# Talos

> A self-hosted AI agent with a deterministic permission kernel. The model proposes tool calls; the kernel decides whether they may execute. Source is public and MIT licensed.

## Source snapshot

- Permission kernel: 913 lines of Python.
- 31 tools in the manifest, gated before dispatch.
- 2623 collected tests in the current source tree; platform-dependent checks may skip.
- 217/217 adversarial cases passed in that source run.
- Published release metrics are separate: https://talos-agent.ch/status.json
- Grants bind one tool call's exact arguments, are single-use and expire after 30 seconds.
- Confined Claude and Codex coding workers. MCP runs in the Claude worker from an operator-owned registry.
- Experimental Computer: persistent ARM64 KVM Linux workspace, headless by default, optional desktop. Available in 0.19.0-alpha; the Computer requires separate provisioning.
- Updates are signed tarballs, verified before unpacking; dependencies are pinned and hashed.

## Pages

- [Home](https://talos-agent.ch/): capabilities, Computer, illustrative chat and kernel demos.
- [Get started](https://talos-agent.ch/setup/): guided terminal or Telegram setup.
- [Documentation](https://talos-agent.ch/docs/): searchable configuration and operation reference.
- [MCP Registry](https://talos-agent.ch/registry/): explicit server examples and worker boundaries.
- [Evidence](https://talos-agent.ch/redteam/): attack categories, case studies and runnable checks.
- [Compare](https://talos-agent.ch/vergleich/): source-linked comparison with OpenClaw and Hermes.
- [Console](https://talos-agent.ch/console.html): illustrative session walkthrough and published release data.
- [Changelog](https://talos-agent.ch/dist/CHANGELOG.md)
